clue.text: His smirk brought about minor conflict

indicators.note: brought about suggests turning round, so the letters of the two opening words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's smug smirk provokes a small scuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' rearranges HISSMIRK; it reads as 'caused', which is exactly the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a brief, small-scale fight between troops, hence a minor conflict.

clue.text: Jars of wine aboard

annotationWithheld.why: Jars of wine aboard (6): the only parse is HOCK inside SS, with 'aboard' as both the SS letters and the containment indicator, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Tell where the pupils are?

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be told the location of the schoolchildren.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, so pupils are 'in form'; 'pupils' might first suggest the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell is to give information; pupils sit in a form, a British school class.

clue.text: Hand control to labour force

parts.note: to hand a post is to man it, staff it
power is control or authority

explanation.surface: Giving authority over to the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' as a verb means 'man' (staff); it looks like the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower is the number of workers available, the workforce.

clue.text: Catches up with weaponry

indicators.note: up in a down light means read from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a net catches, so nets as a verb means catches

explanation.surface: Someone becomes familiar with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down entry reverses NETS; 'Catches up with' reads as one phrase but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a light British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Back in a jiffy

explanation.surface: Someone promises to return very soon.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal is to second it, and a moment or jiffy is a second.

clue.text: They happen to smooth the way up

parts.note: even means smooth or level

indicators.note: up in a down light means read upwards, reversing the letters for way

parts.note: St is street, a way

explanation.surface: Things that come along to make the path easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ST (street) to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are occurrences, things that take place.

clue.text: Too big for one's boots? Go west, tour around north!

indicators.note: around suggests turning things about, so go, the compass letter and tour are mixed up

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for west
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Advice to an arrogant person to head off on a westward trip circling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges GOWTOUR; the idiom 'too big for one's boots' means conceited, but here it is literal: a child's feet outgrow boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots a growing child can no longer fit have been left behind in size, literally too small now.

clue.text: Detachment in action left

indicators.note: in means the detachment word sits inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
a part, as of a force, is a section separated from the whole

explanation.surface: A military unit setting off into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detachment' suggests separation, but here it is a military unit, a section sent off from the main force; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means gone away, set off.

clue.text: Aim, in present situation, to find miscreant

indicators.note: in, completed later by situation, says the word for aim is placed within the word for present
situation finishes the phrase in present situation, saying where the aim word is situated

parts.note: to present something is to offer it
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Sizing up the current state of affairs to track down a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'situation' together say where the aim sits; 'present' looks like 'current' but is the verb meaning give.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who has broken the law.

clue.text: Not being released — fold and replace

parts.note: a fold is a sheep pen
read as re-place, put back: the word put written backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions for folding something and putting it back, while being kept in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' is read literally as 'put back', so PUT is written back to front, giving TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings held in rather than vented are bottled up, not being released.

clue.text: Hide from the real disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Concealing oneself away from genuine trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, which when tanned becomes this material.

clue.text: From wrecked ark, marsupial reaches S African plateau

indicators.note: a wrecked ark is broken up, so its three letters are rearranged

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial

explanation.surface: A kangaroo struggles out of the shattered ark onto a South African upland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' is the anagram signal and turns ARK into KAR; the Karroo is also spelt Karoo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karroo (also Karoo) is the semi-desert tableland of South Africa's Cape interior.

clue.text: Hannibal besieging ancient city, by Don

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the cannibal's surname goes round the city

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: The Carthaginian general Hannibal laying siege to an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannibal suggests the Carthaginian general besieging Rome, but it is Hannibal Lecter of The Silence of the Lambs. A don is a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, one who gives formal talks to students.

clue.text: Frank has heart set on winning her?

parts.note: frank means candid, outspoken

indicators.note: heart means the central letter of the word has

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is determined to woo a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name. Candida is the title heroine of Shaw's play, whom the poet Marchbanks has his heart set on winning from her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shaw's play the young poet longs to win the parson's wife, so she is the woman he is set on.

clue.text: Withdraws and canters off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of canters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A horse retreats and trots away at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CANTERS; the horsey surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to retract a statement or belief, to take it back.

clue.text: Cute chirping sound tails off

indicators.note: tails off means the tail end is dropped, so the bird noise loses its final letter

parts.note: a tweet is a small bird's chirp

explanation.surface: A sweet little bird call that gradually fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails off' removes the last T of TWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or dainty, cute to a cloying degree.

clue.text: Manages meeting with journalists about silver orfe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the journalists go around the fish

parts.note: the press are journalists collectively
the ide, or orfe, is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A chairman meets reporters to discuss a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the containment signal; the ide is a European carp-family fish also called the orfe, whose silver form is the wild type.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair a gathering, being in charge of it.

clue.text: Find there's a record surplus

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means left over, surplus

explanation.surface: Someone learns that a record is too plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to come upon or detect, to find out.

clue.text: A seasoned sailor's sound sense necessary, for storms

indicators.note: the sense of sound, hearing, is needed, so the words must be heard rather than read

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, so a salt's

explanation.surface: An experienced mariner's good judgment is needed in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storms' looks like weather but is the verb, as soldiers storm a position; 'sound sense' reads as good judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it violently by force.

clue.text: Given the artillery I would quickly attack

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: With the guns supplied, an officer says he'd strike fast.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden swift strike on an enemy, so to raid is to attack quickly.

clue.text: Rhyme on poster is inopportune

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the rhyme follows the poster

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement, ad
rhyme is a loose word for verse

explanation.surface: A jingle printed on a billboard turns out to be badly timed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means unfavourable or hostile, ill-timed and working against you.

clue.text: Observe present linked with past in the playground

parts.note: observe in the present tense is see
the past tense of see is saw

explanation.surface: Notice how the present connects with history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' and 'past' name the tenses of 'see'; the definition is a playground fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A teeter-totter, a balanced plank children ride up and down, is found at a park for children.

clue.text: Spiny lizard from Missouri heading for Scottish waters

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A lizard leaves Missouri bound for a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' reads as travel but just sets one piece before the other; the moloch is also called the thorny devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The moloch, or thorny devil, is an Australian lizard covered in spikes.

clue.text: Sub-lieutenant in the band

explanation.surface: A junior officer playing in the regimental band.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet was the lowest commissioned cavalry officer; it is also a brass instrument played in a band.

clue.text: Gets to the top and comes off

explanation.surface: A climber reaches the summit and then falls.
explanation.definitionFit: One who succeeds rises in career or life; a plan that succeeds works out or comes off.

clue.text: Marine worm found by explorer crossing a lake

indicators.note: the explorer crossing a lake is read as his name spanning the letters, which sit inside

parts.note: Marco Polo is the Venetian explorer

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing a lake discovers a sea worm.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller to China.
explanation.definitionFit: The palolo is a Pacific polychaete worm that swarms at the surface to spawn.

clue.text: Unreal silence before midday

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
am, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A false hush in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake, something counterfeit and not genuine.

clue.text: Disrobe girl to her underwear

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone tells a woman to strip down to her undies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest oneself is to strip off, to take off one's clothes.

clue.text: Greeting relative about this is material

indicators.note: about means around, so the family member surrounds the greeting

parts.note: a son is a relative
hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a cousin while discussing some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the containment signal; hallo is an older spelling of hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalloon is a light twilled woollen cloth used for coat linings.

clue.text: Small animal top dog, being worldly wise

parts.note: a shrew is a small mouselike mammal

indicators.note: top here means the topmost letter of the word dog, its first letter in a down light sense

explanation.surface: A little creature becomes leader of the pack through cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' looks like a phrase meaning the boss; it gives just D, the first letter of 'dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute and sharp in practical judgement, worldly wise.

clue.text: Great success unless on the motorway

definitions.text: Great success unless on the motorway

parts.words: Great success unless on the motorway
parts.note: a big hit with the public, except that on a fast road the same words would describe a crash

explanation.surface: Something is a triumph everywhere except on a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: On a motorway (a British highway) a smash and a hit would mean a collision, so the phrase is a triumph only off the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely popular show or record is a runaway triumph with audiences.
